1.title: Night highlights. Mon 31 Aug
1.linkedin:
Sixty seconds of last Thursday at The Triffid.

Five bands, all of them people who build software for a living, and every one of them played like this was the gig they'd been waiting all year for. Rex Software and URBAN X, Epsilon, Jumbo Interactive Limited, Suncorp Group, For The Record (FTR). The room was full before the first band walked on and it stayed loud until the trophy went up.

What we keep coming back to is how good the playing was. These are engineers and product people rehearsing in lunch breaks and after bedtime, and they turned in sets that a lot of working bands would be happy with.

The raffle on its own raised over $3,000 for Youngcare, before we count a single ticket. That money helps young Australians with high care needs live with more choice, freedom and dignity, and it's why we do this.

Proudly powered by Jumbo Interactive Limited, our national sponsor. Thank you to The Triffid, to our judges and crew, and to everyone who bought a ticket and yelled for a band from a company they'd never heard of.

We'll post a reel for each band this week. Sydney is next, 8 October at The Manning Bar.

2.title: ShipReX. Tue 1 Sep
2.linkedin:
Your Brisbane 2026 champions, ShipReX.

Ten people from Rex Software and URBAN X on one stage in full pirate gear, an erhu next to the guitars, bubble wands going in the crowd, and a set that opened on Careless Whisper before dropping into Uprising, ran through Espresso, Dumb Things and Everlong, and finished on Covered in Chrome, a Brisbane song by a Brisbane band, with the whole of The Triffid singing every word of it back at them. They took the biggest crowd vote of the night and the trophy went home with them.

The thing that stood out, once you got past the pirates and the bubbles, was how tight it was for a ten-piece. Plenty of full-time bands can't keep that many people locked in. This lot did it with people who'd been shipping code that afternoon.

3.title: Epsonics. Wed 2 Sep
3.linkedin:
Epsonics, Epsilon's house band, took second place by two points and posted the highest judges' score of the night.

They ran a full Severance theme: walked on out of a blackout to the show's title music with the video behind them, and went straight into No One Knows without a gap. It's My Life, Uptown Funk and Electric Feel got the room moving, When You Were Young sent the arms up, and they closed on The Chain. Keytar on stage. Top marks for visuals from all four judges.

They saved the best for last. The Chain with three voices stacked on the harmonies, then that bass break and a finish as big as the room could take.

4.title: Jumbo Band. Thu 3 Sep
4.linkedin:
Jumbo Band have played every Brisbane Battle of the Tech Bands since the first one in 2022. They won that one, they've been near the top of the scoreboard every year since, and this year they also flew down to play an outstanding guest set at the Melbourne Battle of the Tech Bands.

This year they came third with the top performance score on the night. They walked on as chanting monks in LED masks, dropped the robes for Bring Me to Life, then Beer, a two-minute Never Had So Much Fun, Chelsea Dagger with the crowd doing its part, Say It Ain't So, and a long, chatty build into Take the Power Back to close. Four singers swapping in and out all set, cowbells on the kit, and a projector of their old gigs running behind them. Nobody puts on a bigger show at one of these.

Jumbo Interactive Limited also sponsors the whole event nationally. It says a lot that the sponsor's own band turns up, plays as hard as anyone, and cheers for whoever beats them.

Proudly powered by Jumbo Interactive Limited. Every dollar raised goes to Youngcare, supporting young Australians with high care needs to live with more choice, freedom and dignity.

5.title: Total Loss. Fri 4 Sep
5.linkedin:
Total Loss started when someone at Suncorp Group brought a guitar to team drinks. Twelve years on, this was their first Battle of the Tech Bands.

Back in the U.S.S.R., Gold on the Ceiling, Message in a Bottle, We Can Get Together, Sultans of Swing, and Paint It Black with a sax to finish. Gen-X TV shows rolling on the screen behind them, three guitars including an acoustic, Sultans of Swing built around the lead guitarist, and behind the kit the bass player's 16-year-old son, the youngest person ever to play a Battle of the Tech Bands. They took the top song-choice score of the night from the judges.

No costumes, no concept, just energy. Fourth on the scoreboard, and nobody in the room would have picked it as a debut. Twelve years of playing together shows, and so does having a drummer who's been in the band since before he could drive.

6.title: Off the Record. Sat 5 Sep
6.linkedin:
Off the Record came back to defend the trophy they won in 2025, and they made everyone earn it.

For The Record (FTR) has spent thirty years recording what's said in courtrooms. Their band went full 70s for the night, put two lead vocalists, Becca and Fay, out front and opened on Just a Girl, then Immigrant Song, Barracuda, It's My Life and Never Miss a Beat. In the middle of all that was It's All Coming Back to Me Now, cut down but built entirely around Fay, and she absolutely delivered. That was the performance people were talking about at the bar afterwards.

Fifth on the night on the numbers, but the crowd-vibe score was second only to the winners. Defending is harder than winning and they turned up and did it properly.
